Package com.puppycrawl.tools.checkstyle.checks.coding

Class UnnecessaryPermitsClauseCheck

java.lang.Object
com.puppycrawl.tools.checkstyle.AbstractAutomaticBean
com.puppycrawl.tools.checkstyle.api.AbstractViolationReporter
com.puppycrawl.tools.checkstyle.api.AbstractCheck
com.puppycrawl.tools.checkstyle.checks.coding.UnnecessaryPermitsClauseCheck
All Implemented Interfaces:
Configurable, Contextualizable
public class UnnecessaryPermitsClauseCheck extends AbstractCheck
Checks that a permits clause of a sealed class or interface is not unnecessary, i.e. that it is not possible to omit the clause and have the compiler infer the exact same set of permitted subtypes.

See the Java Language Specification for more information about sealed classes.

This Check does not perform full type resolution. It determines whether a permitted type is local to the file by comparing simple names against every type declaration (class, interface, enum, or record) found anywhere in the compilation unit, including nested and sibling top-level types. As a result, a permitted type whose simple name coincidentally matches an unrelated local type declaration could, in theory, be misidentified as local. In practice this situation cannot occur in code that compiles, since the Java compiler would not be able to resolve such an ambiguous reference in the permits clause.

Since:
14.2.0
